# transformation-workforce

## Edition items

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-w46-nice-qantas-cut-jobs" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-w46/nice-qantas-cut-jobs/" data-aixpm-date="2026-11-10" data-aixpm-title="NICE and Qantas cut jobs months after saying they would not." markdown>

**NICE and Qantas cut jobs months after saying they would not.** NICE will cut about 500 roles (5% of roughly 10,000); its CEO cites R&D teams "leveraging AI tools to increase productivity materially" and the removal of "layers of management and span of control", after saying in July "We have no plans to reduce headcount." Qantas will cut around 850 back-office roles through an Accenture deal that moves most of the work to India first, with automation and AI to follow; its union says it was told earlier this year there was "no plan to offshore any jobs". In both cases the productivity claims are management's own. [CTech, 4 Nov 2026](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/ygubfbd9r) · [Information Age, 10 Nov 2026](https://ia.acs.org.au/article/2026/qantas-to-axe-850-jobs-in-ai-overhaul.html)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-10-microsoft-voluntary-buyouts" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-10/microsoft-voluntary-buyouts/" data-aixpm-date="2026-10-31" data-aixpm-title="Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees while spending $175 billion on AI infrastructure." markdown>

**Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees while spending $175 billion on AI infrastructure.** The offer covers roughly a quarter of the global workforce, at vice-president level and below in the US, UK, Canada and India. Microsoft has not said AI replaces these roles; the link is the timing of the spending. [CBS News, 26 Oct 2026](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/microsoft-buyouts-60000-workers-artificial-intelligence-layoffs/)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-10-bmw-pipedrive-cut-management" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-10/bmw-pipedrive-cut-management/" data-aixpm-date="2026-10-31" data-aixpm-title="BMW and Pipedrive cut management layers with AI as the stated reason." markdown>

**BMW and Pipedrive cut management layers with AI as the stated reason.** BMW plans to remove about 20% of senior management roles by mid-2027, its CFO citing agentic AI as the route to "leaner structures and faster decision-making"; the report does not say how AI absorbs the work. Pipedrive proposed cutting 267 jobs in Estonia, 70% of its local staff, because small businesses now ask AI for software recommendations and its search traffic has "declined sharply". [Business Today, 1 Oct 2026](https://www.businesstoday.in/jobs/story/bmw-to-cut-20-of-senior-management-roles-with-ai-as-it-pushes-for-cost-savings-559029-2026-10-01) · [Estonian World, 1 Nov 2026](https://estonianworld.com/business/estonias-pipedrive-to-cut-70-of-local-workforce-as-ai-disrupts-its-business-model/)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-10-program-manager-roles-cut" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-10/program-manager-roles-cut/" data-aixpm-date="2026-10-31" data-aixpm-title="A program manager reports 40% of PgM and TPM roles cut and not backfilled." markdown>

**A program manager reports 40% of PgM and TPM roles cut and not backfilled.** The practitioner says AI "comfortably takes care of" reporting, documentation and basic communications, "still 20-40% of my week", and expects fewer roles, especially for juniors. It is a single account from an unnamed company. [Reddit r/projectmanagement, 12 Oct 2026](https://www.reddit.com/r/projectmanagement/comments/1x48mon/is_the_saas_pm_world_in_trouble_because_of_ai/)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-09-big-4-leaner-staffing" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-09/big-4-leaner-staffing/" data-aixpm-date="2026-09-30" data-aixpm-title="A Big 4 insider describes projects staffed 50–75% leaner, with AI expected to fill the gap." markdown>

**A Big 4 insider describes projects staffed 50–75% leaner, with AI expected to fill the gap.** A consultant who rejoined a Big 4 firm 18 months ago writes that projects now run with 50% to 75% fewer people than five years ago on the expectation that AI closes the gap, which it does not yet do. The account also reports manager burnout and a partner track that is "all but dead" without multi-million sales. [Reddit r/consulting, 12 Sep 2026](https://www.reddit.com/r/consulting/comments/1weo3tm/leaving_investment_role_at_pe_fund_to_rejoin/)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-08-meta-cancelled-second-wave" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-08/meta-cancelled-second-wave/" data-aixpm-date="2026-08-31" data-aixpm-title="Meta cancelled the second wave of its AI-driven restructuring." markdown>

**Meta cancelled the second wave of its AI-driven restructuring.** Reuters reporting, relayed by IBTimes UK, says Mark Zuckerberg dropped the November phase of "Project OT" the night before the May layoffs, which still cut about 10% of staff. Internal data showed code changes up 220% year on year while features reaching users rose only 36%, and major incidents up 40%. Meta declined to comment on the figures. [IBTimes UK, 27 Aug 2026](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/meta-ai-restructuring-zuckerberg-cancels-layoffs-1816629)

<div class="aixpm-item" id="2026-08-ey-kpmg-want-juniors" data-aixpm-key="/editions/2026-08/ey-kpmg-want-juniors/" data-aixpm-date="2026-08-31" data-aixpm-title="EY and KPMG want juniors back in the office as AI takes over technical work." markdown>

**EY and KPMG want juniors back in the office as AI takes over technical work.** EY's UK head of consulting, Sayeh Ghanbari, told the Financial Times that remote-heavy careers are "just not the route to success in the world of AI" and that flexibility will have to be reduced to build human skills. KPMG's UK advisory head made the same point about juniors learning directly from others. [Scottish Financial News, 27 Aug 2026](https://www.scottishfinancialnews.com/articles/junior-staff-to-return-to-office-to-sharpen-human-skills-as-ai-advances)
